nodes.body: You are sailing your little boat when black clouds roll in fast. The wind howls and the sea turns the color of iron. Do you try to turn back to shore, or ride out the storm where you are?
You spin the tiller hard, but a wave slams the boat sideways and knocks you into the freezing water. Nobody on shore can see you out here.
You grip the mast as the boat is thrown up and over a huge wave, then it flips, dumping you into the churning dark sea.

The water is cold and black, and you cannot see the shore anymore. Your arms are getting tired, and no one is coming. Do you keep swimming toward where you think land is, or hold onto a floating plank and wait?
After what feels like forever, your fingers hit something solid: the hull of a fishing boat. Strong hands pull you aboard. You are shaking, cold, and alive.
You cling to the plank until, hours later, the storm passes and a coast guard boat finds you, half-frozen but breathing.
